rooms.8207: Sacks of meal, a rack of hams and a stack of empty barrels crowd this low cellar room beneath the farmhouse. The walls are plain planking over packed earth, and the air smells of dust, apples and old sacking. Behind the barrels the boards sound oddly hollow when you knock them, as if a false wall hid something better kept out of sight. A ladder climbs up through the trapdoor to the house above.
rooms.8219: A narrow landing at the head of the inn stair, its floorboards worn pale down the middle by travellers' boots. Four stout doors face one another across the little space: a door ahead of you, one to your left, one to your right and one behind you, each with a heavy iron lock. A single candle sputters in a wall sconce, and the smell of bread and ale rises faintly from the common room as the stair winds down toward it. Somewhere beyond a door, a floorboard creaks.
rooms.8223: This is a cramped, tidy chamber with a narrow bed, a travelling chest bound in iron and a stool beside a shuttered window. The coverlet is pulled so tight it might have been ironed, and the whitewashed walls bear not one picture. Look closely at the beam above the bed, though, and you will find a small eye cut into the wood, half hidden by a smear of soot. The only way out is the door back to the landing.
rooms.8224: The room is comfortable enough for a well-paying guest, with a wide bed, a washstand and a rag rug before a small hearth that has not been lit in days. A cheerful sampler about hospitality hangs by the window. The bedding is rumpled, a half-burned candle stands in a puddle of wax on the sill, and the air smells faintly of stale smoke. The door to the landing stands to your left.
rooms.8221: Gundigoot lodges well, for a man who claims to be a simple traveller: the bed is hung with a heavy green curtain, a brass lamp stands on a polished table, and a good carpet hides the boards. A locked coffer sits at the foot of the bed, and a plain cloak hangs on a peg beside the door to the landing. A narrow back stair spirals down toward the warm kitchen, where the heat of the hearth seeps up through the floor.
rooms.8225: Furnok keeps a barer room than his companions: a pallet, a bench and a basin, and the shutters nailed fast against the village outside. Scratches in the plaster by the bedhead form a pattern of crossed lines that is not quite a letter and not quite a pictogram. A stub of tallow burns on the floor, and the air is close and sour. The only door leads out to the landing.
rooms.8220: This hidden chamber lies behind a wall that looks solid from the other side, and it is far too tidy for a mere pantry. Iron-bound chests stand in a row against the stone, each with a lock of better quality than any innkeeper would buy. Dust lies thin on the floor, and a faint oily smell hangs in the air. A narrow way leads on to the larger store room, and a stair climbs up to the inn above.
rooms.8222: Barrels of ale, kegs of salted pork and crates of crockery fill this long store room beneath the inn, stacked high and hung with cobwebs. A single oil lamp in a niche throws shadows over the beams, and the floor is damp where the casks sweat. One wall is oddly thicker than the rest, with a seam running down it that looks too straight for age. A stair rises up to the kitchen, and a narrow way leads toward a hidden chamber.
rooms.8241: The upper hall of the church is long and silent, lit by narrow windows glazed in thick, greenish glass. Oak beams curve overhead, and the floorboards are polished by the soft shoes of priests. Doors stand at either end, one to the quarters of the priest's assistant and the other to the chief priest's chambers, each with an iron latch. A plain stair leads down to the vestry, and a lingering smell of beeswax and incense hangs in the air.
rooms.8243: A small, ordered chamber, with a narrow bed, a writing desk under the window and a shelf of well-thumbed prayer books. The assistant cleric keeps his things neat, and a simple wooden symbol of Helver hangs above the pillow. The room smells of ink and lamp oil. Something about the ceiling is wrong, though, for a faint pattern of scratches has been cut into the corner plaster, as if someone had drawn the same small mark over and over. The door leads back to the hall.
rooms.8244: Rich hangings of crimson and gold cover the walls of this chamber, and a great bed stands on a low dais beneath a canopy of embroidered silk. A heavy desk, a carved prayer stool and a silver lamp suggest comfort far beyond a village priest's means. The shutters are closed tight, and the air is warm and a little too sweet. Behind the hangings you glimpse the edge of a hidden recess, and the door out to the hall stands at your back.
rooms.8242: The Sacred Trophies Gallery is a long, dim loft under the church roof, where glass-fronted cases line the walls and the rafters hang with faded banners. Chalices, reliquaries and crumbling scrolls of old victories lie on velvet, each tagged in a careful hand. The floor creaks softly underfoot, and the light is dusty and amber. A steep stair climbs up to the study and audience chamber.

8223.description: An eye no bigger than your thumb is carved into the beam, its pupil blackened with soot. It is cut so neatly that it could only be the work of a patient hand, and it faces the bed.
